=== ROOT REQUIREMENTS.md ===
# Mine

Mine is a set of PWAs (Progressive Web Apps) to digitalize ones personal or professional life.
The key idea is to save everything in a repo as markdown files. This can be calendar entries,
diaries, markdowns extracted from voice recordings / pdfs / .. These .md files can easily be
ported to new apps without a vendor lock-in and are processed via an (AI) assistant to help you
plan your day, keep track of tasks, remind you of memories a.k.a. a second brain.

To keep complexity to a minimum each use-case lives in a separate folder. e.g. the calendar PWA
lives completely in a 'calendar' folder as does the zettelkasten and all the other apps. Each
folder contains a 'sample' folder with samples how the markdowns shall look, a REQUIREMENTS.md
describing how the PWA works and a TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md describing how it is built.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for how this is built.

## One app, one setup

Mine installs as **one** app on the phone, with one icon. The apps in the subfolders are pages
inside it, not separate installs.

This is what makes the central requirement work: **the GitHub repo and token are entered once,
in the main app, and every app in a subfolder uses them.** Verified on iPhone and Android.

## Main app

A tile per app: its `icon.svg` above its folder name.

Above the tiles, apps may contribute a summary. The calendar's shows today's entries and the
next one — which matters, because opening the app is the only reminder that works (see below).

## First run

1. Open the app URL and add it to the home screen (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen;
   Android: menu → Install).
2. The setup screen asks for GitHub owner, data repo, branch, and a personal access token.
3. The app tests the connection and reports clearly if it fails.

Settings are stored on the device only. The token is never displayed again after entry, and the
app warns 14 days before it expires.

Two settings belong to Mine rather than to any one app, and the same two rows appear in the main
settings and in each app's: **theme** (system, light or dark) and **date format** (auto, which
follows the device's locale, or `dd.mm.yyyy`, or `mm/dd/yy`). Both default to following the
device, so Mine looks like the rest of the phone until you say otherwise.

## Using it

- Changes appear instantly and are queued for GitHub in the background.
- A sync indicator shows: in sync / pending / error.
- Offline, the queue is kept and sent when you are back online or reopen the app.
- Editing the same entry on two devices never loses either version: the other device's version
  keeps the file, yours is kept beside it and flagged, and the sync indicator tells you there is
  something to review. Nothing is discarded and nothing is silently overwritten — but the app
  does not interrupt you to ask which to keep, because by then you are somewhere else.
- Everything works offline, including dates and search, because the app keeps a full local copy.

## Reminders

**Mine cannot notify you while it is closed.** No browser can schedule a notification for later;
this is a platform limitation, not a missing feature. Alerts are stored with each entry and
exported, and they fire while the app is open. The summary on the tile screen is the reminder.

## Updates

When a new version is deployed the app shows "Update ready — reload". It never updates while you
are in the middle of editing.

The banner appears only when the version waiting to take over genuinely differs from the one
running. A new worker can sit waiting while being identical to the active one, so "a worker is
waiting" is not the test — if it were, the banner would appear on an app with no update at all
and never go away. Reloading twice with no deploy in between must leave no banner.

## Privacy

Your data lives in a **private** repo. The app itself is public, but it contains no data, and the
token is scoped so that it can only touch the data repo.
=== CALENDAR REQUIREMENTS.md ===
# Calendar

Calendar is an app of [Mine](../REQUIREMENTS.md) to manage your calendar. Every entry is one
markdown file in the data repo, so your calendar stays readable and portable without this app.

See [TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) for the file format.

## What an entry holds

A title, a type — **event** or **task** — a start and end, a group, a location, participants,
alerts, and a free markdown body for the agenda, checklist or notes.

A task also carries a **stage** — `todo`, `doing` or `done` — and, optionally, a priority (1, 2
or 3) and an estimate in days. An event has none of the three. Stage is the only record of a
task's progress; there is no separate done flag.

Entries can repeat, and a repeating entry can have single occurrences skipped, moved, retitled
or moved to another stage without affecting the rest.

## Layout

A navigation pane at the top and a big calendar window below it.

In the top pane, from left to right:

- Left/right buttons to move to the previous/next day, week, month, year or sprint, depending on
  the current view.
- The current day/week/month/year, with a small downward arrow for a dropdown date picker. The
  dropdown shows a month at a time, with its name top left and left/right arrows top right.
  Clicking the month name switches to a year grid of 9 years ending with the current one, whose
  arrows page by 9 years. In the kanban view the label reads `Sprint 7 · 19 Jan – 1 Feb` and the
  dropdown picks a sprint.
- A button to jump to today.
- A dropdown to filter by group. Each group shows its colour. This is a view filter and is
  remembered per device; groups are *named and coloured* in settings, not here.

# Calendar — technical requirements

File format and rendering for [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md). Sync, caching and writes are
in [../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](../TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Paths

```
calendar/2026/04/2026-04-18-1400-k3f9.md     one-off entry
calendar/2026/04/2026-04-25-0000-ov1q.md     occurrence override
calendar/recurring/trash-p7qm.md             entry with a recurrence rule
calendar/groups.md                           group -> colour and label
calendar/settings.md                         kanban anchor and interval
```

The whole folder is mirrored locally, so the path is not a loading optimisation. It is for
humans: the repo browses chronologically on github.com, and no directory grows past a month of
entries. `-k3f9` is 4 random characters, **not** a counter — two devices creating entries offline
on the same day must never mint the same name. No title slug, so retitling is never a rename.

**The path is never the source of truth.** It is derived from `start` at creation; after a move
or an override the two can disagree. Always read `start`. Changing an entry's date is a rename,
which is a delete plus a create in one commit.

Entries with a `recurrence:` rule live in `recurring/` rather than the date tree, because an
open-ended rule must render in months it was not created in and there is no month folder to find
it under.

## Frontmatter

RFC 5545 (iCalendar) naming wherever one exists, so `.ics` export is close to a field copy.
**Empty keys are omitted, never written as `None`** — `None` is a YAML string, not null, and a
parser hands back the text `"None"`.

| Key | Applies to | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | both | required |
| `type` | both | `event` or `task` |
| `start` | both | `DTSTART`. A bare date (`2026-04-18`) is all-day; a timestamp (`2026-04-18T14:00:00Z`) is an instant |
| `end` | both | same value types as `start`; omitted when a single all-day item |
| `group` | both | a name, resolved through `groups.md` |
| `stage` | `task` only | `todo` / `doing` / `done`. Replaces the old `done` boolean |
| `priority` | `task` only | `PRIORITY`, 1-9. The UI writes 1-3, and those three read back unchanged; a hand-written 4-6 reads as 2 and 7-9 as 3 |
| `estimate` | `task` only | days. Ours, no RFC 5545 equivalent |
| `location` | both | free text |
| `alerts` | both | minutes before start, `0` = at start. Stored and exported only; nothing fires in the background |
| `participants` | both | list of email addresses |
| `recurrence` | both | RRULE string, e.g. `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=SA` |
| `exdate` / `rdate` | recurring | occurrences to skip / extra occurrences |
| `status` | override | `cancelled` removes the occurrence. The only value used |

depth of the layout:

```graphql

  ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
    ... on Tree { entries { name type object {

        ... on Blob { oid text isTruncated } } } } } } } } } } }
```

  A 16 MB / 145 file response came back in 6 s without error.
- `Blob.oid` is byte-identical to the REST tree SHA, so this single request also supplies the
  SHAs that pulls diff against and writes send as their base.

disk, all paths relative so the `/mine/` prefix needs no config.

`shared/apps.js` exports the app list and is imported by both the tile screen and `sw.js`, so
adding an app means editing one array. An app may export `summary()` from `widget.js`.

## Bootstrap — 1 request

One GraphQL query returns an app folder's tree **with contents and blob SHAs**, nested to the
depth of the layout:

```graphql
repository(owner:$o, name:$r) { object(expression:"main:calendar") {
  ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
    ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
      ... on Tree { entries { name type object {
        ... on Blob { oid text isTruncated } } } } } } } } } } }
```

- `rateLimit.cost` is **1** however many files return — `entries` is not a paginated connection.
  A 16 MB / 145 file response came back in 6 s without error.
- `Blob.oid` is byte-identical to the REST tree SHA, so this single request also supplies the
  SHAs that pulls diff against and writes send as their base.
- Check `isTruncated`: GraphQL truncates very large blobs and returns `text: null` for binary.
  Fall back to a REST blob fetch for that path.
- An **empty repo** returns `object: null` rather than an error, and `defaultBranchRef: null`.
  Treat it as an empty mirror, not a failure.

**Do not use the tarball.** `GET /tarball/{ref}` 302-redirects to `codeload.github.com`, which
answers `access-control-allow-origin: https://render.githubusercontent.com` — one specific
foreign origin. `fetch()` applies CORS to the final response after the redirect, so it is
blocked, and the preflight an authenticated request needs returns 403. `api.github.com/graphql`
by contrast sends `allow-origin: *` and a 204 preflight allowing `Authorization`.

**A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright.** Not just the ref read — `POST
/git/blobs` itself answers 409 "Git Repository is empty", so there is nothing to build a tree
from. Only `PUT /contents/{path}` can create the first commit. The first queued file goes that
way, and everything after drains normally once a history exists.

## Pull

1. `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{branch}` with `If-None-Match`. A 304 means nothing changed and
   costs no rate-limit quota.
2. On 200: fetch the tree, diff blob SHAs, fetch only changed files, drop deleted paths.

Run on app open and on window focus. Background Sync does not exist in Safari, so all syncing is
foreground.

## Writes — one commit per drain

Queue each change locally with the blob SHA it was based on, then drain the whole queue as one
commit via the Git Data API: `POST /git/blobs` per file, `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`
(deletion = entry with `sha: null`), `POST /git/commits`, `PATCH /git/refs/heads/{branch}` with
the expected old SHA and **no force**.

One drain is one commit, so a move — delete plus create, because the date is in the path and the
API has no rename — cannot be half-applied, and a 20-item offline backlog is one commit.

A rejected ref update means someone pushed elsewhere: pull, rebuild on the new base, retry. This
succeeds, because nearly every write is a create at a freshly generated path.

**True conflict** = a queued change whose base SHA no longer matches the remote blob. Remote keeps
the canonical path; the local version is committed beside it as `<name>.conflict-<yyyymmdd>.md`
with `conflictOf:`. Nothing is discarded and the queue never jams. On 401/403, pause and send the
user to settings.

## Service worker

Registered `{type: 'module'}` so it can import `shared/apps.js`. A version constant names the
cache; install precaches the shell. Same-origin requests are cache-then-revalidate.

Requests to `api.github.com` **bypass the worker entirely** — caching an API response would hand
back a stale ETag and silently break sync.

A new worker waits; the UI offers "Update ready — reload" and `skipWaiting()` runs only on tap.

**The offer is gated on the version, not on a worker waiting.** The worker answers a `version`
message over a `MessageChannel` port with its `VERSION` constant, and the page compares the
waiting worker's answer with the active one's; equal answers mean no banner. A worker that is
byte-identical to the running one can sit in `waiting` indefinitely, and `reg.waiting` alone as
the condition is what makes the banner appear on an app with no update and never go away. A
worker too old to answer reports `null` after a 1.5 s timeout, which differs from a real version
and so still offers the update.

## Token and CSP

Stored plaintext in IndexedDB with its expiry: as safe as the unlocked device. The threat that
matters is injected script on our own origin, closed off by policy rather than encryption:

```
default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' https://api.github.com
```

**No CDNs, ever.** Dependencies are committed to `/shared/vendor/`, pinned by hand, with source
URL and version in `VENDOR.md`. The token is never written to a log, a URL, or the DOM.

The OAuth device flow is not an option: GitHub's `login/device/code` endpoints send no CORS
headers, so a fine-grained PAT is the only no-backend path.

## Dependencies

| What | Why not hand-rolled |
| --- | --- |
| `js-yaml` | Files are hand-edited and must parse as real YAML — quoting, multiline scalars, flow maps. A subset parser misreads them silently. |
| `rrule` | `FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR` and DST-crossing weeklies are where hand-rolled expansion is wrong without telling you. |

YAML *writing* is ours (~20 lines): we control the output shape, so no dumper is needed.

**Load with `CORE_SCHEMA`, never js-yaml's default.** The default is YAML 1.1 and parses
`start: 2026-04-18` into a JS Date at UTC midnight — silently shifting every all-day entry by a
day east of UTC. `CORE_SCHEMA` keeps it a string and still handles bools, numbers, flow maps and
quoted scalars. This is the same off-by-one the bare-date format exists to prevent, arriving
through the parser instead.

`spike/res/`.

| | Result |

expectation is why the one-app topology was chosen.

content.text:
Found the mechanism. A timed entry's line is `[14:00] [title] [tick]`, and `.when` and `.tick` are both `flex: none`. The month grid is `repeat(7, 1fr)`, which is `minmax(auto, 1fr)` — a cell can't shrink below its content's minimum, and `.day` has no `min-width: 0`. So seven cells each insist on roughly 3.5rem, plus the week gutter: ~430px of demanded width on a 360px screen. It only misbehaves when entries are *timed*, which is why desktop looks fine.

Note that `calendar/REQUIREMENTS.md` describes a month line as *"small lines carrying the title"* — it never mentions a time. The code adds one.

**What I grilled you on, and where it landed**

| Your point | What it collided with | Resolution now in the docs |
|---|---|---|
| `E` for estimate | `E` was already the event half of the type toggle (`popup.js:154`) | `T` stays a letter; event becomes a drawn calendar icon |
| Remove the task row | Priority lived in that row and nothing was said about it | Priority joins as `P` — `S` `P` `E` right after the type pair |
| — | *"Each of the six field buttons opens its own popup"* | `S` and `P` cycle in place, only `E` opens one; stated as an explicit exception |
| — | *"An icon whose field is set is shown enabled"* — stage is always set, so `S` would always be lit and the row would stop summarising | These three show their **value** instead (stage colour, priority digit on its chip colour, `2d`); the lit rule is scoped to the six field icons |
| — | *"An event has none of the three"* | Hidden on an event, not greyed |
| estimate = 1 | *"optionally … an estimate in days"* and *"Empty keys are omitted"* | A clearable prefill, so `estimate` can still be absent; "optionally" stands |
| tasks always todo | Already the behaviour (`popup.js:80`) | Pinned as an explicit default; no code change needed |
| green save / red trash | — | Root `REQUIREMENTS.md`, as a Mine-wide convention; the calendar inherits |
| Android overflow | Nothing — it violates requirements that already exist | New hard rule: every view fits 320 CSS px, kanban swipe is the only sideways movement |

**The month-view diagnosis** (worth keeping, because it was the actual bug): a timed entry's line is `[14:00] [title] [tick]`, and both `.when` and `.tick` are `flex: none`. The grid is `repeat(7, 1fr)` = `minmax(auto, 1fr)`, and `.day` has no `min-width: 0`, so each cell demands its min-content width — roughly 3.5rem — and seven of those plus the week gutter ask for ~430px on a 360px screen. Desktop never shows it. That drove the decision that a phone month line carries the title alone; the fix itself is `min-width: 0` on the cell plus dropping `.when` under 600px.

Two things I did **not** do, since you asked only for the docs:

- No code changes. `popup.js`, `ui.js`, `views.js`, `index.html` and both stylesheets still describe the old design.
- No change to either `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md` — I checked, and nothing in them contradicts these decisions (the frontmatter table already has `estimate` as optional, which the clearable-prefill answer preserves).

One correction to your point 2: there's no `adb` here, so your phone isn't reachable from this machine. When you want the implementation, I'll verify with local chromium at 320 and 360 px against `calendar/sample/` — which already contains timed entries, the case that overflows — and you confirm on the Android after.
